Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
1018 AM EDT Thu Sep 10 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Coastal Flood Advisory has been issued for Havre de Grace until
11am this morning. Marine Weather Statement issued for 20 kt 
west to southwest gusts over the lower waters through 12pm. 
Monitoring bands of light showers mainly west of I-81 this 
morning. The bulk of this activity will decay as it pushes east 
of the mountains this morning while remaining along and south of
I-66/US-50. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- 1) A slow moving cold front brings the risk of shower and a few 
thunderstorms to the region through early Friday morning.

- 2) Scattered shower and thunderstorm chances continue through
  the weekend with drier conditions early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...A slow moving cold front brings the risk of shower and a few 
thunderstorms to the region through early Friday morning.

A mid to upper jet streak will bring forcing along a surface cold 
front as it drops southeastward over the next 36 to 48 hours. This 
combination of a jet and surface front will initiate additional 
showers and a few thunderstorms along and on the north side of the 
front primarily mid afternoon into the overnight tonight. The line 
of heavy showers and storms that moved from southwest PA into 
western MD late last evening and overnight has since weakened 
considerably and is now a broken line of showers in northeastern WV 
and north-central VA. 

A strong mid to upper jet will swing by to the north today into 
tonight and put us in the right entrance. This would indicate good 
upward motion with developing convection later today into tonight. 
The greatest CAPE will likely be around 1000-1500 J/kg across 
central VA where the most heating and highest low- level moisture 
content is anticipated.
 
Some storms may tend to cluster heading into this evening given 
forcing along the front and increased flow aloft, but the modest 
CAPE/DCAPE should keep any severe weather threat rather limited for 
wind and hail. Still, can't rule out a briefly stronger, more 
organized rotating storm in the vicinity of the front/wave in the 
evening across central VA to southern MD.

The front will slowly but steadily drop southward heading into 
Friday. Some shower activity may linger or redevelop in the vicinity 
of the front near the I-64 corridor, but most of the time/area 
should be dry Friday unless the front slows down much more 
significantly.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Showers and thunderstorms possible on Sunday,
followed by drier conditions early next week.


A weak cold front meanders through the forecast area beginning 
Saturday morning into Sunday, resulting in a few possible 
thunderstorms in the afternoon into the evening. While chances for 
these storms to be severe remain low, a few strong storms with gusty 
winds cannot be ruled out. Otherwise, on and off showers continue 
throughout the day Saturday and into Sunday as the front moves 
through.

Come Monday, upper level ridging starts building over the East Coast 
accompanied by surface high pressure overhead. Primarily dry 
conditions are expected on Monday, although an isolated rain shower 
cannot be ruled out along the western portions of the forecast area 
as a cold front tracks across the Great Lakes. Precipitation chances 
increase by midweek as another cold front tracks across the forecast 
area.

High temperatures will be in the 80s for most (70s mountains) each 
day with high humidity values yielding heat indices in the low 90s 
for those east of the Blue Ridge. Wednesday will be the warmest day 
with highs in the upper 80s to low 90s and heat indices in the upper 
90s.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions are expected amongst the terminals through 
this evening. Temporary reductions are possible at times this 
afternoon and evening due to scattered showers and thunderstorms. 
Highest confidence for afternoon showers and storms appears to be 
from a line south of CBE/MRB to BWI/MTN. Locations further south 
toward IAD, DCA and CHO have a better opportunity for showers and 
thunderstorms given the placement of shortwave energy rolling 
through. Out of these three locations the greatest opportunity for 
thunderstorms exists at terminals south of I-66/.US-50 this includes 
IAD/CHO where filter breaks of sunshine are likely to break through. 
Thunderstorm development would likely occur between 20-01z/4-9pm. 
Coverage will be isolated to scattered with more scattered to 
widespread shower activity overnight as the front swings through. 
Went with PROB30s to encompass the afternoon shower and 
thunderstorms threat with prevailing showers this evening based on 
current guidance. Beyond the showers and thunderstorms, not looking 
at a whole lot of low clouds nor fog outside the mountains. Skies 
will remain between SCT-BKN this afternoon trending BKN-OVC this 
evening as the front pushes in. MAV/MET guidance continues to hold a 
high likelihood of low cigs/vsbys mainly west of Blue Ridge heading 
into Friday morning. This will be something to monitor in subsequent 
TAF cycles. Any temporary restrictions this evening into early 
Friday morning will give way to VFR conditions Friday afternoon as 
brief dry air moves into the region. A leftover shower or 
thunderstorm is possible from KCHO south Friday afternoon and 
evening as the front stalls nearby.

Additional scattered showers and thunderstorms are possible during 
the afternoon/evening hours this weekend. This will lead to 
temporary reductions amongst the terminals at times otherwise VFR 
conditions will prevail. South to southeast winds Saturday will 
switch to the west and southwest winds Sunday at less than 15 kts. 
Winds turn to the north and northwest Monday and Tuesday as VFR 
conditions continue. 

&&

.MARINE...
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the lower waters of 
the Chesapeake Bay and tidal Potomac through 12pm. Showers and a few 
thunderstorms are anticipated later this afternoon into tonight. A 
few Special Marine Warnings are possible especially south of 
Washington DC to Annapolis MD. Winds shift to the west and northwest 
today as a cold front crosses, then shift to north and east through 
Friday as the front stalls to the south. Winds shift to southerly on 
Saturday with southerly channeling yielding Small Craft Advisory 
criteria winds in the afternoon. 

West winds on Sunday shift to northerly on Monday, remaining below 
SCA criteria each day. Showers and an isolated thunderstorm are 
possible over the waters on Sunday, although SMWs are not
likely.


&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tide levels remain elevated (0.5 to 1 ft above normal)this morning 
at Havre de Grace with a Coastal FLood Advisory through 11am. More 
notable water level decreases will occur tonight behind a cold 
front, before levels increase again this weekend.


&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...Coastal Flood Advisory until 11 AM EDT this morning for MDZ508.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 10 AM EDT this morning for ANZ534-
     537-543.

&&

$$
